title: 149 Tiny Speakers, One Very Loud Wall
summary:
What happens if you link 149 tiny speakers together? A team at WIRED found out by building a literal wall of sound at its London office. The speakers were IKEA's Kallsup, a $10 Bluetooth speaker launched in April. Each one is a 2.75-inch cube in bright white, green, or pink, and IKEA had said it might be possible to chain 100 of them.

WIRED asked IKEA's headquarters in Almhult if it could try. IKEA agreed and raised the challenge, saying it might be possible to link up to 150 without breaking the connection, so it sent 150 speakers. "No one has ever tried this, though," an IKEA spokesperson said. "We haven't." One speaker was damaged in shipping and rattled, so the team worked with 149.

Chaining them was simple. After pairing one Kallsup with an iPhone 16 Pro, the team powered on another cube while music played and held down Play until a chime signaled "multi-speaker" mode. Linking all the speakers took about 30 minutes.

Each Kallsup has a single 1.8-inch driver powered by a 3-watt amplifier, with Bluetooth 5.3 support and no separate tweeter or woofer. On its own, it sounds fine, though a bit tinny, and works well as a small desktop or bedside speaker. With 149 drivers, the combined surface area roughly equals one enormous 22-inch driver, and the combined rated output is 447 watts.

At 100 speakers, the sound was seriously loud, like a fire alarm rather than a hi-fi system. At maximum volume with all 149, the team could not hear each other speak and could feel vibrations, and the music lost clarity. Still, the chain kept working. The experiment fell well short of the world record of 1,500 speakers set by Majority Audio in March 2026. At modest volumes, the wall sounded more composed, though the music lacked depth. A wall costs $1,490, and WIRED does not recommend buying one. Its lesson was simple: for high-quality audio, buy a better speaker. For $10, the Kallsup is simple, easy to chain, and hard to fault.
why_it_matters: The experiment shows that linking many cheap gadgets can produce an eye-catching result, but more of something is not the same as better quality, a useful lesson when choosing tech.

background_read: A Bluetooth speaker is a small speaker that plays music sent wirelessly from a phone or another device, without a cable.
A driver is the part inside a speaker that vibrates to make sound, and an amplifier boosts the signal so the sound comes out louder.
Chaining speakers means linking many of them so they all play the same music at once, which can make the sound much louder but does not always make it sound better.
The experiment tested how far a chain of cheap speakers could go before the connection broke.
